description:
We prove that the classical two-colour Langton ant exits every square of side n within (13/4) 3^n + 4 updates, uniformly over all initial colourings and internal poses. For a rectangle with N columns and fixed height H, we obtain an upper bound of order N^(floor(H/2)+1). Rational potentials on the critical curve (a-1)(b-1)=4 have positive monomial increments: four-step costs give the square estimate, while pairing along the short direction gives the rectangular bound.

A related strict rational clock yields decidable complete-state reachability, two-sided orbit equivalence and a computable orbit normal form. The analytic proofs are accompanied by independent exact Laurent-polynomial checks, exact rational tests, finite-state audits, and Lean 4.30.0 proofs of the supercritical local clock and telescoping lemmas. The eight-page manuscript and self-contained source archive include the critical-potential implementation, retained evidence, reproduction commands and SHA256 manifests.

Version 0.3.0 strengthens version 0.2.0 by removing the factor n from the earlier square bound and adding fixed-height rectangular estimates. It belongs to the same preprint version chain.
title: An Ant on the Clock: Exponential Escape Bounds for Langton's Ant
